Title: Admin MFA can be bypassed using a password step token
Proposed_change: Give admin pre-auth tokens a separate purpose and audience. Require a completed admin session, exact staff subject, active account, and current database role on every admin endpoint. Remove email-based identity fallback and all frontend preAuth-to-adminToken fallback.
Acceptance_criteria: Password-step, student, refresh, expired, revoked, malformed and wrong-audience tokens must fail every privileged route. Valid MFA-completed staff can access only permitted roles.

Title: Production initialization installs a publicly recoverable default admin password
Proposed_change: Remove production demo staff seeding. Use an explicit one-time bootstrap command with a randomly generated credential and mandatory enrollment. Never reseed staff because an unrelated exam table is empty. Check existing installations for seeded accounts, rotate affected credentials and invalidate their sessions.
Acceptance_criteria: A fresh production database creates no predictable accounts automatically. Emptying exam data never recreates or resets staff. Bootstrap is auditable and cannot be silently repeated.

Title: Public password reset changes administrator credentials before ownership proof
Proposed_change: Replace this with an enumeration-resistant reset request that sends a short-lived single-use reset link. Change the password only after verified redemption. Use per-account and per-IP limits and revoke sessions after a successful reset.
Acceptance_criteria: Unknown and known emails receive equivalent public responses. The existing password remains usable until verified reset completion; failed delivery never changes it.

Title: MFA enrollment and OTP handling weaken the second factor
Proposed_change: Require an existing verified factor or a separately controlled recovery procedure for MFA replacement. Never return or log OTPs in any production response. Enforce durable challenge limits, account/IP throttling, single-use verification and recent reauthentication.
Acceptance_criteria: Pre-auth alone cannot replace an enrolled factor. Simulated mail failure returns no OTP. Repeated verification and login attempts hit account limits and secrets never appear in logs.

Title: Admin data endpoints have missing or ineffective authentication
Proposed_change: Apply one hardened admin authentication and authorization guard across all modules. Define which roles may read drafts, operations, telemetry and audit data. Add route-level negative tests instead of relying on hidden navigation.
Acceptance_criteria: Anonymous, invalid-token, student and inactive-staff requests fail. Each permitted role has explicit read and write coverage for every /admin route.

Title: Test attempts have no reliable identity ownership or entitlement boundary
Proposed_change: Require a student access session, ACTIVE status, valid test entitlement, and attempt owner on every start/resume/sync/submit/result request. If guest practice is intended, design a separate constrained guest identity rather than a shared stu_anon account.
Acceptance_criteria: Student B cannot read, alter, sync or submit student A’s attempt. Anonymous and suspended accounts fail. Non-entitled users cannot start locked tests.

Title: Access and refresh tokens are interchangeable and session revocation is incomplete
Proposed_change: Separate token verification by purpose/audience and implement hashed rotating refresh sessions with replay detection and revocation. Require ACTIVE status during login and all protected requests. Use the current database role for staff privileges.
Acceptance_criteria: Access tokens cannot refresh. Replayed refresh tokens fail. Logout, suspension, password reset, role change and revoke actions invalidate the intended sessions.

Title: Mobile login and onboarding do not match the real profile API
Proposed_change: Choose one canonical profile contract and explicitly map database records to it. Validate request and response DTOs at boundaries. Persist primary exam, settings and target minutes. Store pre-login onboarding choices locally and apply them after verified sign-in.
Acceptance_criteria: New and returning users complete sign-in/onboarding against apps/api, retain settings after restart, and can change exams and language without runtime errors.

Title: Mobile test runner and answer synchronization do not match the API
Proposed_change: Unify start, question and sync DTOs. Add real API contract tests using the actual mobile client. Return per-question acknowledgments including accepted client sequence and server deadline. Preserve backward compatibility only through explicit, tested adapters.
Acceptance_criteria: The shipped mobile client can start, resume, answer, clear and mark review using the real API. Each successful response passes its shared schema; sync acknowledgments match the versions stored.

Title: Submission results and the result retrieval route are incompatible
Proposed_change: Implement an authenticated owner-only result route and persist the complete result snapshot. Return the canonical result schema for both submit and retrieval. Use null and an explanatory note for unavailable rank data.
Acceptance_criteria: A submitted result renders immediately, after app relaunch and on another signed-in device. No solutions or correct options are disclosed before authorized submission.

Title: Reported success does not mean data was saved to PostgreSQL
Proposed_change: Introduce awaited repository create/update/delete methods with explicit error propagation and transactions. Persist each domain mutation before acknowledging success. Use an outbox for related audit/worker operations. Avoid whole-database process-local caches as the authority.
Acceptance_criteria: After every mutation, a second process and a cold API restart see the same state. SQL failure returns an error without a false success or cache-only change. Concurrent writers cannot overwrite newer state.

Title: Production database fallback can create a separate unmounted data store
Proposed_change: Fail startup in production when the configured PostgreSQL database is unavailable. Make embedded mode explicitly development/test-only. Report the selected database mode and readiness truthfully, and test backup restoration to a separate database.
Acceptance_criteria: Disconnect PostgreSQL in a staging production-mode stack: API must not become ready on another database or seed a new identity store. Restore tests recover users, attempts and content.

Title: Demo purge clears all records in selected tables
Proposed_change: Remove or disable this action in production until data is explicitly tagged by provenance. Restrict deletion to demo IDs within a transaction, preview counts, require recent authentication and preserve a restorable backup.
Acceptance_criteria: Real records survive a demo purge. Server-side validation rejects broad flags without scope. A rollback and audit record are available for the exact deleted fixture set.

Title: Test deadlines resume and section locks are not enforced by the server
Proposed_change: Snapshot the test and marking rules at start, persist expiresAt, implement explicit resume, enforce section windows and terminal transitions transactionally, and derive remaining time from server deadlines with a defined offline grace policy.
Acceptance_criteria: Backgrounding, clock changes, relaunch, late sync and concurrent submit cannot extend time or change a final score. Section transitions and marking follow the selected published exam version.

Title: The document upload and preview flow is a simulation
Proposed_change: Implement actual multipart or staged object upload with byte/size/type checks, real SHA-256, persisted object identity and private storage. Add safe PDF/image rendering and a sandboxed DOCX conversion worker. Implement a real download/open flow and enforce distribution policy at the server.
Acceptance_criteria: Upload a real sample of each supported type, restart, preview actual content and download byte-identical permitted files. Corrupt, oversized and disallowed files fail; restricted originals are not publicly accessible.

Title: Many admin pages are disconnected demonstrations
Proposed_change: Connect each screen to authenticated API queries and mutations. Build missing create/edit/publish/provision/broadcast endpoints with validation and persistence. Remove fake success, fabricated counts and implied guarantees until implemented.
Acceptance_criteria: For each visible action, browser automation observes the intended API request, a durable database change, a truthful failure state, and the resulting student-facing change after refresh.

Title: Current affairs ingestion and scheduled publishing do not perform their stated work
Proposed_change: Implement allowlisted RSS retrieval with timeouts, redirects/DNS checks, safe XML parsing, deduplication, source evidence and an editorial state machine. Make durable scheduled jobs catch up after downtime. Display the same published records across web/mobile.
Acceptance_criteria: A controlled test feed creates drafts once, approved scheduled content appears at the expected time, rejected content stays private, and a restarted worker catches up without duplicate publication.

Title: Exam verification records do not apply proposed changes
Proposed_change: Persist versioned proposals and evidence. Require a matching pending proposal, separate active reviewers and a validated diff. Apply the approved revision and audit entry atomically, and serve one canonical exam dataset.
Acceptance_criteria: Self-approval, missing/cross-exam/already-reviewed proposals fail. A valid second reviewer changes the published exam version and the same details appear on web and mobile.

Title: Mail can report success while sending nothing and disables TLS verification
Proposed_change: Use an explicit test-only mail mock. Validate SMTP configuration independently of HTTP API credentials and fail production readiness on missing required settings. Restore TLS certificate validation. Handle delivery failures honestly, queue retries where appropriate and avoid resetting credentials on send failure.
Acceptance_criteria: A staging delivery reaches an actual test inbox. Incorrect SMTP credentials and an invalid TLS certificate fail clearly; production never reports mock delivery as real delivery.

Title: Email quota controls are neither daily nor durable
Proposed_change: Persist atomic per-provider/per-day send reservations with provider reconciliation and priority for OTPs. Add truthful actual/estimated labels and configure provider-side spending limits independently.
Acceptance_criteria: Quota survives restart and multiple workers, rolls over on the documented day boundary and applies to every mail path. Exceeding the cap blocks lower-priority sends without fabricated dashboard status.

Title: CMS HTML is rendered without a sanitization boundary
Proposed_change: Sanitize allowed CMS markup on the server, restrict URL protocols and dangerous tags/attributes, and add a suitable web Content Security Policy. Move staff sessions to server-managed HttpOnly Secure cookies or a BFF pattern, with CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated mutations.
Acceptance_criteria: Stored script/event-handler/javascript-URL payloads do not execute. Staff credentials are inaccessible to page scripts; legitimate rich content and authenticated writes continue to work.

Title: OTP persistence stores plaintext and does not persist attempt counters correctly
Proposed_change: Store keyed OTP digests, enforce one active purpose-bound challenge or an explicit challenge ID, update attempts/consumption atomically, and encrypt TOTP secrets with a separate managed key. Keep test-only OTP inspection outside production code.
Acceptance_criteria: Concurrent checks cannot reuse a code, restart cannot reset attempt limits or resurrect old codes, and database/log exports do not reveal usable OTP/TOTP secrets.

Title: Offline synchronization can acknowledge the wrong answer revision
Proposed_change: Acknowledge and compare exact versions, maintain per-attempt queues, rerun a drain when new work arrives, and flush on reconnect/app foreground. Surface native persistence failures and use explicit recoverable storage states. Namespace and clear student caches appropriately on account changes.
Acceptance_criteria: Delay the first sync response while changing an answer twice: the latest sequence must reach the server and remain pending until acknowledged. Reconnect and relaunch recover unsent work, and storage failure never shows Saved Locally.

Title: APK builds do not establish a stable release signing identity
Proposed_change: Configure a stable protected release keystore or managed EAS/Play signing, unique increasing Android versionCode and a verified production API URL during the actual JS bundle step. Publish only after required CI and a signed APK upgrade test.
Acceptance_criteria: Install release N, then install N+1 without uninstalling: the same signer is verified and user data survives. Debug-signed, unsigned or untested builds cannot be published as official releases.

Title: Mobile production API selection and update metadata have multiple authorities
Proposed_change: Use one validated environment/config source and fail release builds on localhost/HTTP API URLs. Publish one immutable signed release descriptor with versionCode, signer and checksum; persist server release settings. Clearly describe the updater as a download prompt unless full verified download/install is implemented.
Acceptance_criteria: Inspect the final release bundle and run it on a physical device against the intended HTTPS API. Restart retains the selected release metadata; update links and version fields agree.

Title: Build and test configuration gives incomplete quality assurance
Proposed_change: Include the mock tool in workspace or remove the dependency on it, add actual contract test scripts, and run production API integration tests. Pin one supported Node/pnpm toolchain, use frozen-lockfile installs without fallback, and require successful type/build/security/E2E gates before releases.
Acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout installs and runs every advertised command under the pinned toolchain. Web, mobile and API are tested together. CI rejects DTO drift, invalid tokens, persistence failures and release-signing mistakes.

Title: API test setup can delete local non-test database directories
Proposed_change: Allocate a unique disposable database/directory per test run, reject production mode and real database paths, and delete only the owned test resource in teardown. Use a real second process to test restart persistence.
Acceptance_criteria: Place a sentinel in a normal local data directory and run tests: it survives untouched. Parallel runs use distinct databases and neither truncates the other’s fixtures.

Title: Deployment and migration procedures can announce success after failure
Proposed_change: Build and verify images before replacement, take/verify backups before schema changes, apply migrations under a lock with explicit transactional policy, and fail readiness on initialization errors. Require health and functional smoke checks with nonzero failure exit codes and retain previous image tags.
Acceptance_criteria: A broken build leaves the previous service running; failed health checks fail deployment; two simultaneous starters do not apply a migration twice; a documented rollback restores the previous known-good state.

Title: Public content and personalized progress are largely static
Proposed_change: Derive progress from authenticated student records, persist tasks and read status, and connect all published content to canonical APIs. Show honest empty/stale states and explicit demo labels. Require editorial source checks before any Official or Verified claim.
Acceptance_criteria: Two students see their own real progress, task changes survive restart, unpublished material is excluded, and empty production data never becomes fabricated activity or current news.

Title: Server rendered CMS pages ignore the configured internal API address
Proposed_change: Centralize server-only API configuration with consistent /v1 normalization, and use it for SSR. Route all editable system pages through the same publication rules and define preview/revalidation behavior.
Acceptance_criteria: With documented Compose defaults, create/edit/publish a CMS page and verify its actual public HTML. Internal addresses are not exposed to clients, and a legitimate unpublish removes cached public content within the stated policy.

Title: Security monitoring and rate limiting have misleading gaps
Proposed_change: Configure only known proxy hops, use durable per-account and per-IP auth throttles, align telemetry schemas and recursively redact allowlisted metadata. Use a maintained history-aware secret scanner and verify rotation of previously exposed provider credentials without copying them into reports. Add actionable health/worker alerts.
Acceptance_criteria: Proxy tests preserve client limits without spoofing. Real mobile telemetry is accepted, sensitive nested metadata is removed, and provider-side rotation plus incident checks are recorded.

Title: Public route metadata and accessibility need a focused cleanup
Proposed_change: Keep one robots source, remove nonexistent routes, include published CMS pages and real modification dates, and generate metadata from validated page fields. Run keyboard, mobile viewport, contrast and screen-reader checks on actual rendered screens.
Acceptance_criteria: All sitemap URLs resolve intentionally; robots and metadata are consistent. Login, dialogs, tables and navigation work at phone widths and by keyboard with visible focus.

Title: Dependency audit reports unresolved advisories in the locked stack
Proposed_change: Triage each advisory against actual runtime imports, enabled features and platform. Upgrade framework/plugin groups together to supported patched versions, update the lockfile reproducibly and run contract, auth, SSR, native and deployment tests. Do not blindly apply a forced audit fix or mark every advisory dismissed because basic flows work.
Acceptance_criteria: Save an advisory-by-advisory applicability record with affected version, feature prerequisites, fix or documented mitigation, then rerun the registry audit. No reachable critical/high issue remains without an explicit assessed mitigation.
